target_customer: Mobile app product and engineering teams at publishers, media and consumer apps
problem: Mobile teams could not reliably A/B test native iOS and Android apps or roll out changes without a full app store release.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for mobile A/B testing, feature flags and staged rollouts

founders.name: Nancy Hua
founders.background_notes: Described by TechCrunch (July 2013) as an expert algorithmic trader in finance.

founders.name: Jeremy Orlow
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder by TechCrunch at launch; not listed on the YC page.

competitors.name: Leanplum
competitors.what: Mobile testing startup targeting game developers

competitors.name: Pathmapp
competitors.what: Mobile testing startup targeting game developers

competitors.name: Clutch.io
competitors.what: Small mobile testing service acquired by Twitter

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed SDKs for iOS and Android that apply experiments reliably in native apps, plus statistics and a visual editor; solid engineering but not research-grade.

defensibility.rationale: SDK integration created some lock-in, but rivals such as Optimizely and Taplytics launched mobile testing and the product was largely replicable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Optimizely, Mixpanel and Taplytics launched mobile testing by 2015; Apptimize remained independent and sold to Airship in August 2019.

market_need_then: TechCrunch noted in July 2013 that existing A/B vendors focused on web and that companies relied on weak in-house tools; the founders said top apps shipped updates many times daily.

identity.voice_and_tone: Company About page says the team questions its beliefs and welcomes feedback.

rebrands.why: Continued as a standalone product after the acquisition

brand_strength.rationale: Launch and funding coverage but no press about the brand, no mascot or community found; the name is a blend of app and optimize.

outcome_analysis: Apptimize entered mobile A/B testing at launch in July 2013 when most testing vendors served the web, raised about $18.5 million through a $12.4 million Series B in 2016, and grew to customers such as The Wall Street Journal and Strava. Optimizely and others added mobile testing, and the company sold to Airship in August 2019 on undisclosed terms with about 19 staff joining, a mid-sized strategic exit.
notes: Total raised $18.5M stated by TechCrunch in 2016 and matches the rounds. Andreessen Horowitz appears in the seed investor list in the TechCrunch seed article. Education of founders not found. Series A lead per TechCrunch is Costanoa; one aggregator differs. Airship acquisition terms undisclosed; about 19 staff joined per press summaries.
